title: How Zara Really Makes Money (The €40 Billion Machine)
description:
Inditex, the company behind Zara, sold almost €40 billion of clothes in fiscal 2025 and made a record €6.2 billion profit — while spending next to nothing on traditional advertising. In this file we open the money machine behind Zara: a 14-year-old delivery boy in A Coruña, the shop that was meant to be called Zorba, the two-to-three-week design-to-shelf system, why the store itself is the advert, where the revenue really comes from, the founder's €3.2 billion dividend, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Inditex fiscal 2025 annual results and first-half 2026 results (as reported by FashionUnited, Inside Retail Asia and GlobalData/Retail Times); Retail Gazette; Ara ("Fifty years of Zara"); Britannica; Wikipedia (Zara); Procurify; LongYield.

All figures are from company results where available and are rounded. The online share of sales is our own arithmetic. The share of clothes made near Spain and the design-to-shelf time are widely reported estimates, not exact company figures. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
